rows.decision: Keep participant-level random split and basic MFCC/CNN/metadata pipeline as reference.
rows.evidence: MFCC/logistic and RF reached around 0.75-0.80 AUROC; fusion around 0.88.
rows.outcome: Useful baseline but not enough to address professor concern about low single-modality numbers or SOTA comparisons.

rows.decision: Add strict temporal holdout, time-stratified split, month label/covariate shift, and month ablation.
rows.evidence: Temporal AUROC dropped from 0.873 to 0.566 in earlier stress test; month removal improved metadata temporal AUROC by 0.247.
rows.outcome: Strong reliability story: collection month acts as shortcut.

rows.decision: Replace simple LR-only baseline with extended acoustic features and multiple learners with SMOTE/Optuna/fusion.
rows.evidence: Strong internal AUROC reached about 0.891 but not >0.90 consistently.
rows.outcome: Improved internal numbers but did not create SOTA-level evidence.

rows.decision: Fine-tune WavLM-base-plus branches on segmented cough/breath/speech.
rows.evidence: Cough and breath test AUROC stayed around 0.79 on practical run.
rows.outcome: Stopped as unproductive for timeline; evidence that heavier model alone was not enough.

rows.decision: Try PSO-style feature subset search and gated prediction stacking.
rows.evidence: PSO validation objectives around 0.73-0.77; gated stack test around 0.891, not materially above strong baseline.
rows.outcome: Not final headline; retained only as negative/rescue evidence.

rows.decision: Extract standardized OpenSMILE ComParE2016 and IS10, merge with strong features, select top-k by LightGBM.
rows.evidence: Final internal selected result reached AUROC 0.897; paper-style CV cough 0.819 and speech 0.806.
rows.outcome: Best final internal pipeline; still below SOTA papers but cleaner and more reproducible.

rows.decision: Run existing participant split, time-stratified split, strict temporal split, and COUGHVID external transfer on the final feature strategy.
rows.outcome: Final defensible research result: strong internal performance does not survive external transfer.

rows.paper_result: Development AUROC 0.691 on COVID-19 Sounds and 0.668 on Coswara; postdevelopment AUROC 0.607 and 0.597.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Explicitly targets temporal drift; notes Coswara adaptation was less consistent due changing prevalence, symptoms, age/gender biases; UDA assumes source-target similarity and AL needs reliable labels.
rows.what_we_did: Built time-stratified and strict early-to-late temporal evaluations; monthly label/covariate shift tables; temporal month causal audit; uncertainty under shift; final ComParE+IS10 temporal stress test.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not implement UDA or active learning; did not validate newer variants with prospective deployment data.
rows.primary_source: P1_jmir_drift_adaptive.pdf/text lines around Discussion and Principal Findings.

rows.paper_result: BLSTM COVID/non-COVID classifier reported AUC 91.5% with subgroup bias/fairness analyses.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Future extension: enlarge subject count and increase diversity across demographics, gender, age, and health conditions; metadata can expose bias.
rows.what_we_did: Used Coswara as source dataset; participant-level splits; quality audit; metadata confounding; temporal/month shift; subgroup and residual SMD analyses.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not collect new subjects or improve demographic diversity; dataset limitations remain inherited.

rows.paper_result: Dataset paper; cough detector ROC area 0.97; expert diagnosis agreement poor (Fleiss kappa about 0.0031).
rows.limitation_or_future_work: COUGHVID labels are noisy; private test set for independent evaluation; metadata such as age/gender may be needed as context.
rows.coverage: Covered for external stress / partially for label noise
rows.what_we_did: Ran final Coswara-to-COUGHVID external transfer on 8,331 cough samples; also earlier COUGHVID internal baselines for MFCC/eGeMAPS/BEATs/PANNs.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not use private COUGHVID evaluator; did not repair expert-label noise; external transfer remains weak.
rows.primary_source: P4_coughvid_arxiv_2009.11644 text Technical Validation/Inter-Rater Reliability/Private Set.

rows.paper_result: Audio ROC-AUC 0.846 before matching; after matching on symptoms/demographics ROC-AUC about 0.619; symptoms often outperform audio in replication.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Recommends metadata dissemination, recruitment-bias control, matching, targeted test sets, expected utility, and out-of-study replication.
rows.what_we_did: Metadata-only classifiers, IPW-controlled audio evaluation, residual SMD tables, matched temporal cohort, external COUGHVID transfer, calibration and operating-point reports.
rows.remaining_gap: Residual unmeasured confounding remains possible; no randomized/prospective cohort.

rows.paper_result: ENCL-DNN AUROC 0.834 on Coswara and 0.854 on Cambridge; ECE improved from 0.178 to 0.089 on Coswara.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Emphasizes reliable probability calibration and uncertainty, not only AUROC.
rows.what_we_did: Every model bundle reports Brier, ECE, NLL; calibration-under-shift and prevalence recalibration analyses included.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not implement ENCL-DNN itself; external probabilities still poorly calibrated without prevalence correction.

rows.paper_result: Reports over 90% AUC for COVID detection; HST outperforms CNN/RNN/transformer baselines on Cambridge/COUGHVID tasks.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Not a diagnostic test; future work should compare with antigen tests, support mobile/cloud deployment, standardize recording procedures, validate broader cohorts/diseases, and add explanation/uncertainty.
rows.what_we_did: Included deep spectrogram/CNN branches, SSL WavLM attempt, multimodal cough/breath/speech fusion, temporal/external validation, and uncertainty/calibration tables.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not reproduce HST architecture; no mobile/cloud implementation; no antigen-test comparison; no broad multi-disease cohort.

rows.paper_result: Accuracy 89.30%, AUROC 94.74%, PR 91.62% using symptom-assisted attention.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Acknowledges confounders age/gender/symptoms; future work: other respiratory diseases and additional multimodal data.
rows.what_we_did: Used symptoms as confounding/audit variables rather than as diagnostic input; quantified symptoms-only AUROC 0.932 to show risk of shortcut learning.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not build symptom-assisted classifier; no multi-disease validation.

rows.paper_result: RF with ANOVA-selected OpenSMILE features reported accuracies 76.47%, 75.54%, and 75.54% for vowels /a/, /e/, /o/.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Handcrafted OpenSMILE only; performance sensitive to feature selection; future deep end-to-end, larger/diverse speech samples, optimization, XAI.
rows.what_we_did: Added OpenSMILE ComParE2016 + IS10; LightGBM feature ranking top-800; paper-comparable speech 10-fold CV AUROC 0.806; feature selection tables.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not train raw-audio end-to-end speech model to completion; no XAI beyond feature attribution.

rows.paper_result: Strategy 5 reports DNDF AUC 0.92 on Coswara, 0.93 on COUGHVID, 0.97-0.99 on other settings; combined dataset AUC/accuracy about 0.97.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Limitations include threshold-moving clinical mismatch, no temporal validation on newer variants, no deployable healthcare evaluation, no cough-specific subtype annotations; future calibration, interpretability, external stability, multi-class disease classification.
rows.what_we_did: Adopted feature selection, SMOTE model bank, threshold tuning, cross-dataset transfer, calibration metrics, final temporal validation, and external stability evidence; did not copy DNDT/DNDF.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not beat their internal AUCs; did not implement DNDT/DNDF; no multi-class disease task; no clinical deployment.

rows.paper_result: Methodology/review style evidence for respiratory screening pipeline concerns.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Calls for subgroup robustness/fairness, mobile noise/microphone variability, device-invariant features, domain adaptation, external validation, nested/repeated subject-level evaluation, and ablations.
rows.what_we_did: Quality audit, domain-shift audit, CORAL baseline, external COUGHVID validation, paper-comparable CV, temporal validation, ablation summaries.
rows.remaining_gap: No device-invariant learned representation that fixes transfer; no full formal ablation of every preprocessing component.

rows.paper_result: Reports prior related works with cough AUC up to 0.98, breath 0.94, speech 0.92; its own texture analysis reaches high binary cough accuracy in a controlled setting.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: States method is not standalone diagnostic; more data/classes and variant/asymptomatic coverage are needed.
rows.what_we_did: Multimodal cough/breath/speech, broad acoustic descriptors, external transfer, temporal shift; we avoided standalone diagnostic claim.
rows.remaining_gap: No new controlled clinical collection; no multi-class respiratory disease extension.

rows.paper: Audio feature ranking for COVID respiratory audio, 2021
rows.paper_result: Feature ranking improved accuracy up to 17% on Cambridge and 10% on Coswara; 88% and 77% accuracy reported.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Future: regularize different sample lengths and identify informative features for deep architectures; generalize to other respiratory diseases.
rows.what_we_did: Implemented LightGBM/ExtraTrees/univariate selection, top-k ComParE+IS10, feature importance/selection artifacts, model-bank comparisons.
rows.remaining_gap: Did not solve variable-length modeling with a dedicated event architecture; no other respiratory diseases.

rows.paper_result: ResNet50 AUC 0.98 on Coswara; LSTM transfer to Sarcos improved from AUC 0.779 to 0.938/0.94 after SFS.
rows.limitation_or_future_work: Requires more stringent validation on larger data and regulatory approval; future: enlarge dataset, transfer learning, smartphone implementation.
rows.what_we_did: External validation and feature selection were performed; no regulatory/deployment claim made.

rows.title: A Comprehensive Drift-Adaptive Framework for Sustaining Model Performance in COVID-19 Detection From Dynamic Cough Audio Data
rows.method: Cough audio, mel spectrograms, VGGish features, chronological splits, MMD drift detection, CUSUM alerts, UDA and active learning
rows.reported_results: Development AUROC 69.1% on COVID-19 Sounds and 66.8% on Coswara; postdevelopment AUROC dropped to 60.7% and 59.7%; UDA improved balanced accuracy by roughly 10%-20%
rows.main_limitation: Focuses on temporal drift; limited interpretation of causes, cross-dataset drift, and interdemographic variability; cough-only
rows.how_ours_compares: We add Coswara-to-COUGHVID cross-dataset transfer, metadata confounding, operating points, and calibration-under-shift, but do not implement full UDA/active learning

rows.title: Coswara: A respiratory sounds and symptoms dataset for remote screening of SARS-CoV-2 infection
rows.datasets: Coswara: 2635 individuals, 23,700 recordings, about 65 hours, 9 sound categories
rows.method: Crowdsourced cough, breath, vowel, and counting recordings plus symptoms and metadata
rows.reported_results: Dataset paper; not a model leaderboard in our comparison table
rows.main_limitation: Crowdsourced recordings and metadata-driven label associations require careful quality and confounding analysis
rows.how_ours_compares: We use Coswara as the core source dataset with participant-level split, quality checks, metadata audit, and representation comparison

rows.title: COVID-19 Sounds: A Large-Scale Audio Dataset for Digital Respiratory Screening
rows.method: Large-scale respiratory audio dataset with participant metadata
rows.reported_results: Dataset reference; raw access requires request/data agreement
rows.main_limitation: Not instantly available for this implementation; cannot be required for reproducibility
rows.how_ours_compares: We cite it for field context but rely on public Coswara plus COUGHVID for executable validation

rows.title: The COUGHVID crowdsourcing dataset
rows.datasets: More than 25,000 crowdsourced cough recordings; more than 2800 expert-labeled recordings
rows.method: Crowdsourced cough collection with metadata, cough detection, and quality tools
rows.reported_results: Dataset paper; expert agreement was limited for some labels
rows.main_limitation: Noisy labels and crowdsourced quality make it an external robustness target, not perfect ground truth
rows.how_ours_compares: We use COUGHVID only as external validation/internal baseline context and report weak transfer honestly

rows.title: Audio-based AI classifiers show no evidence of improved COVID-19 screening over simple symptoms checkers
rows.datasets: UK COVID-19 Vocal Audio Dataset with PCR-referenced cough, exhalation, and speech
rows.method: Audio classifiers compared against symptom/checker baselines under realistic evaluation
rows.reported_results: Main conclusion: audio models may not outperform simple symptom checkers under realistic evaluation
rows.main_limitation: Shows that apparent audio performance can reflect confounding signals, symptoms, and sampling differences
rows.how_ours_compares: We add metadata confounding audits, symptom/demographic/protocol-only models, IPW-controlled audio evaluation, and conservative claims

rows.title: Confidence-Calibrated Clinical Decision Support System for Reliable Respiratory Disease Screening
rows.method: MFCC features, DNN, ensemble-based confidence calibration, LIME-style interpretability
rows.reported_results: ENCL-DNN AUROC 0.834 on Coswara and 0.854 on Cambridge; ECE reduced by 50.0% on Coswara and 28.74% on Cambridge
rows.main_limitation: Mostly cough-focused and not a full external shift/confounding pipeline
rows.how_ours_compares: We include calibration metrics, Brier/NLL/ECE, calibration-under-shift, and avoid interpreting external probabilities as calibrated risks

rows.title: COVID-19 Detection From Respiratory Sounds With Hierarchical Spectrogram Transformers
rows.datasets: Crowdsourced respiratory sound datasets with cough and breathing sounds
rows.method: Hierarchical Spectrogram Transformer with local-to-global attention
rows.reported_results: Reports over 83% AUC for COVID-19 detection from respiratory sounds
rows.main_limitation: Compute-heavy transformer architecture; not necessary for BTech reproducibility
rows.how_ours_compares: We compare modern learned embeddings through BEATs/PANNs and keep the main contribution on reliability rather than architecture novelty

rows.title: SympCoughNet: symptom assisted audio-based COVID-19 detection
rows.datasets: UK COVID-19 Vocal Audio Dataset; 72,999 participants and 25,766 PCR-positive cases reported in project notes
rows.method: Log-mel spectrograms, CNN backbone, symptom-encoded channel attention, augmentation, VAD/noise preprocessing
rows.main_limitation: Symptom-assisted performance can be dominated by symptom metadata rather than audio-specific signal
rows.how_ours_compares: We use symptoms as confounding/audit metadata rather than central diagnostic input

rows.title: Speech-based respiratory diagnostics: A study on COVID-19 detection with machine learning
rows.method: ITU-T P.56 normalization, OpenSMILE 1582-dimensional features, RF/SVM/Decision Tree/ANN, feature selection
rows.reported_results: Random Forest with ANOVA-selected features; accuracy around 76.47% for vowel /a/ and 75.54% for /a/+/o/
rows.main_limitation: Speech-only performance is moderate and task-specific
rows.how_ours_compares: We prioritize cough plus representation robustness and keep speech-biased wav2vec2 as lower priority for the current cough transfer story

rows.title: Robust COVID-19 detection from cough sounds using deep neural decision tree and forest: A comprehensive cross-datasets evaluation
rows.datasets: Cambridge COVID-19 Sounds, Coswara, COUGHVID, Virufy, NoCoCoDa
rows.method: Deep Neural Decision Tree/Forest, RFECV, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, SMOTE, threshold moving
rows.reported_results: AUC around 0.92 to 0.99 across individual settings; combined DNDF reports accuracy/AUC around 0.97
rows.main_limitation: Cough-only and method-heavy; high reported metrics may depend on dataset construction and tuning
rows.how_ours_compares: Our external transfer is far weaker but more conservative; we emphasize calibration/confounding and do not claim comparable SOTA accuracy

rows.title: Audio-Based Screening of Respiratory Diseases
rows.method: Event-focused respiratory audio preprocessing and segmentation pipeline
rows.reported_results: Used for methodology guidance rather than direct COVID metric comparison in current docs
rows.main_limitation: Broader respiratory screening, not directly reproduced here
rows.how_ours_compares: We include quality filtering and note event segmentation as a future extension beyond current global feature extraction

rows.title: Sensors 2022 systematic review on audio-based COVID/respiratory screening
rows.datasets: Review across COVID and respiratory audio studies
rows.method: Systematic review of preprocessing, models, metrics, and study designs
rows.reported_results: Review source; no single directly comparable metric
rows.main_limitation: Review-level evidence cannot validate our model directly
rows.how_ours_compares: We follow the review's multi-metric and preprocessing-documentation guidance

rows.title: COVID-19 detection in cough, breath and speech using deep transfer learning and bottleneck features
rows.datasets: Coswara, ComParE, Sarcos and related respiratory audio data
rows.method: Deep transfer learning and bottleneck features across cough, breath, and speech
rows.reported_results: AUC about 0.98 for cough, 0.94 for breath, and 0.92 for speech
rows.main_limitation: Older high metrics require careful comparison because validation/control assumptions may differ
rows.how_ours_compares: Our results are lower, but we add external COUGHVID transfer, confounding checks, calibration, and operating points

rows.title: Pay Attention to the Speech
rows.method: Handcrafted audio features, class imbalance handling, attention/fusion over speech and respiratory sounds
rows.reported_results: Used as speech/fusion precedent in project docs; exact metric extraction deferred to full paper table
rows.main_limitation: Fusion can degrade if not calibrated and leakage-safe
rows.how_ours_compares: We compare fusion against best single modality and add calibration/quality/confounding evidence

rows.title: Audio texture analysis of COVID-19 cough, breath, and speech sounds
rows.source_year: Biomedical Signal Processing and Control / Frontiers, 2022
rows.datasets: Cambridge COVID-19 Sounds subset: 1141 cough, 392 breath, 893 speech samples
rows.method: Audio texture and handcrafted spectrogram features
rows.reported_results: 5-class accuracy around 71.7% cough, 72.2% breath, and speech binary accuracy around 79.7%
rows.main_limitation: Dataset-specific feature-engineering results; exact binary comparisons need full table extraction
rows.how_ours_compares: We include handcrafted MFCC/OpenSMILE baselines and learned embeddings, then test external robustness

rows.title: Audio feature ranking for sound-based COVID-19 patient detection
rows.datasets: Cambridge and Coswara in project notes
rows.method: Feature ranking and selection for classical sound-based COVID detection
rows.reported_results: Supports feature-selection improvements; exact table metrics not captured in current docs
rows.main_limitation: Feature-ranking evidence does not by itself solve external transfer or confounding
rows.how_ours_compares: We use feature strategies and shift-based feature selection, then report weak external generalization honestly

rows.title: Investigating Feature Selection And Explainability For COVID-19 Diagnostics From Cough Sounds
rows.datasets: DiCOVA challenge context in project notes
rows.method: High-dimensional acoustic features, log-mel CNN, probability-score fusion, explainability/feature selection
rows.reported_results: Reported DiCOVA challenge improvements; exact metrics not captured in current docs
rows.main_limitation: Explainability is inspection, not proof of causal COVID biomarkers
rows.how_ours_compares: We use feature selection and evidence tables, but avoid causal biomarker claims

rows.title: COVID-19 cough classification using machine learning and global smartphone recordings
rows.datasets: Coswara and Sarcos/South Africa smartphone cough recordings
rows.method: Machine learning/deep residual architecture on global smartphone cough recordings
rows.reported_results: Highest AUC around 0.98 from residual architecture in paper highlights
rows.main_limitation: Real-world smartphone recordings introduce device/noise/domain variability
rows.how_ours_compares: We directly show that cross-dataset robustness is difficult and keep device/noise/domain-shift limitations explicit
